design_source: WHO_Recommended_INN_List_91 (WHO Drug Information Vol.38 No.1, 2024), English chemical name for 'mivelsiran'
notes: [sequences] DUPLEX. sequence_5to3 holds the ANTISENSE/GUIDE strand (23 nt) per the dataset convention; SENSE strand (21 nt) = GGCUACGAAAAUCCAACCUAA. ps_count 8 = 4 PS on the sense strand + 4 on the antisense strand; all other linkages phosphodiester. Delivered intrathecally and CNS-targeted by a 2'-O-hexadecyl (C16) lipid anchor at sense position 6 - NOT GalNAc, hence conjugate=lipid. Antisense position 7 is a glycol-nucleic-acid (GNA) thymine (INN: '1-de-beta-D-ribofuranosyl-1-[(2S)-2,3-dihydroxypropyl]-5-methyluridylyl', flanked by non-canonical (5'->2') and (3'->3') linkages) and antisense position 1 carries a 5'-(E)-vinylphosphonate on a 2'-O-methyl uridine. VALIDATION: the INN List 91 entry gives NO molecular formula (it uses a structural diagram instead), so the length could not be confirmed by phosphorus count. It was instead confirmed two other ways - (a) the guide strand is the exact reverse complement of the sense strand over the 21-nt core, treating T as equivalent to U for base pairing (the two T positions are the DNA thymidine and the GNA thymine); (b) the base-pairing schematic printed in the same INN entry independently spells the sense strand GGCUACGAAAAUCCAACCUA... and the antisense ...CCGAUGCUUTUAGG..., both matching this parse, and its own legend uses T for those residues. The WHO source text contains a typographical error at one linkage ('P-thiouridylyl5'->3')', missing an opening parenthesis) which the parser tolerates. ALN-APP identity/target from NCT05231785 (study id ALN-APP-001) and NCT06393712 (ALN-APP-002, CSF sAPPalpha/sAPPbeta endpoints); phase 2, Alnylam.
